acceptance.expected: CI rejects a commit with a file matching secret patterns (`*.pem`, `.env`, the PEM private key header string from the plan)
acceptance.actual: check_secrets.py reports ANY occurrence of a PEM private key header (five dashes, BEGIN, optional words, PRIVATE KEY; case-insensitive, no trailing dashes needed) anywhere in any file, including UTF-16 and binary. File-name patterns are matched case-insensitively. Exceptions: in the exact path docs/implementation-plan-v1.md only ONE quoted fragment (backtick + header + backtick, built in code) is removed once before the scan, because AC-M0-04 in the plan quotes the header; the rest of the plan is scanned as usual (cycle 3; before, the whole file was exempt). Plus two pinned historical (path, Git blob SHA) pairs for cycle-1 reports already in the pushed branch history; any other content at those paths is scanned. tests/ci/test_check_secrets.py: 49 tests, incl. new: plan with the quote passes; plan with the quote plus a second quote / header with key body / RSA header with body / inline key fails; plan with a header and body but no quote fails. Mutations: whole-file exemption back -> 6 tests red; removing every quote instead of one -> 2 tests red. Branch scan origin/main..HEAD and tree HEAD: clean.
evidence: CI job `secrets`: tree of HEAD + every commit of the PR/push; on force-push (unreachable push.before) scans origin/main..HEAD with a notice

HISTORICAL_BLOB_ALLOWLIST pins two cycle-1 report blobs (reports/conformance/M0.json fcc7ad0, reports/critic/M0-cycle-1.json 8bcef75) that quote the AC header. Without it the PR scan of this branch would be red forever, and fixing it would require rewriting pushed history, which the process forbids. Reports from now on must not spell the header out.
The secret scanner is pattern-based (names + PEM private key headers); it does not detect arbitrary API tokens. A full scanner (e.g. gitleaks) can be added later.
connectors/demo tests run standalone without the root conftest policy (network guard, skip ban); the root run applies it. Stated in connectors/demo/pyproject.toml.
CODEOWNERS does not block the merge (owner's decision), and for the owner's own PRs GitHub requests no review at all (the author is never asked); see AC-M0-03 escalation.
The secret scanner does not look inside compressed files: a gzip/zip of a PEM key passes (not required by AC-M0-04).
